title: Semantic Preprocessing Pipeline — common artifact schema
description: The one schema every adapter converges on (see /CLAUDE.md, 'Common schema'). This is what proves reusability is real: adding a new artifact type means writing an adapter that produces this exact shape, not inventing a new one. Validated in practice by tests/test_schema_conformance.py against real output from all three adapters (spreadsheet, document, diagram) — not just written to look plausible.

artifact.description: Human-readable title for this artifact — in practice the source file's stem (e.g. 'budget_test', 'invoice_born_digital').

kind.description: Which family of adapter produced this. Not an enum on purpose: CLAUDE.md's whole reusability claim is that a new adapter (a 5th artifact type, say) can introduce a new kind value without touching this schema. Currently produced values: 'spreadsheet', 'document', 'diagram'.

adapter.description: Which adapter produced this, e.g. 'Spreadsheet adapter'. Human-readable, shown directly in the UI's live-processing panel ('routed to: <adapter>').

regions.description: The extracted content, in reading order. Every adapter's four output shapes (text/structured/json/table — see adapters/common/outputs.py) are pure reshapes of this one array; nothing downstream re-extracts from the source file.

checks.description: Artifact-level sanity checks, independent of any single region's confidence (CLAUDE.md's guardrail: a failed check is not the same as low confidence — both are tracked, never collapsed into one signal).

path.description: Filesystem path to the original source file, as given to the adapter.

hash.description: sha256 of the exact source file bytes, prefixed 'sha256:'. Real provenance, not a placeholder — recomputed from the file every run (adapters.common.schema.sha256_of_file), never cached or trusted from a prior run.

adapter_version.description: The producing adapter's own version string, e.g. '0.1.0'.

id.description: Unique within this artifact. Convention varies by adapter but is always locational: 'Sheet!A1' (spreadsheet), 'page1!block3' or 'page1!ocr-line2' (document), 'node-1'/'edge-1' (diagram) — an id always tells you roughly where in the source this region came from.

type.description: Semantic role, adapter-defined (e.g. 'header', 'formula-cell', 'line-item', 'node', 'edge'). Deliberately not an enum here either, for the same reusability reason as 'kind'.

shape.description: Visual/structural hint. Only diagrams currently set this ('node', 'node-decision', 'node-circle', 'edge'); every other adapter's regions carry null, since the concept doesn't apply.

language.description: BCP-47 language code when detected from real text content (langdetect, a real statistical model — never guessed or defaulted to a fixed value). null when not applicable: non-text regions, structured/tabular content where 'language' is a category error, or text too short to detect reliably.

confidence.description: Real extraction certainty, backed by an actual signal from that adapter's parser/detector/OCR engine — never a hardcoded constant chosen to look reasonable. What the signal actually is varies by adapter and is documented in each adapter's README (e.g. spreadsheet: formula resolution tier; document: text-layer-present vs. OCR engine confidence; diagram: polygon-approximation cleanliness for nodes, arrowhead-density asymmetry for edges).

text.description: Human-readable content. null for a genuinely non-text region (a diagram node/edge with no OCR'd label, a scanned page Tesseract couldn't process) — never an empty string standing in for 'nothing here.'

relationships.description: Real structural links to other regions in this same artifact, e.g. formula-ref / cross-sheet-ref (spreadsheet), sums-line-items (document), connects-to (diagram, exactly two per edge: [from, to] in that order — adapters.common.outputs._table_diagram relies on this ordering).

target.description: The id of another region in the same artifact's regions array.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of what was actually checked and what was found — real values (e.g. 'independent sum=4980, formula value=4980'), not a static message that's the same whether the check passed or failed.
